newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Lebanon gross reserves rise in end-August.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Lebanon gross reserves rise in end-August.

text.p: Bank of Lebanon's gross foreign exchange reserves rose by $49.5 million in the second half of August to $5,024 million, according to the central bank's bi-monthly balance sheet issued on Tuesday.
Gross reserves rose by $38.42 million in the first two weeks of August to $4,974.49 million.
The central bank, the Bank of Lebanon, said the gross reserves rose mainly due to its purchases of foreign currency "to safeguard monetary stability".
Gross reserves include commercial banks' foreign exchange deposits with the central bank.
The balance sheet did not give the Bank of Lebanon's net reserves, which stood at $2,858 million at the end of 1995 compared with $2,732 million at the end of 1994.
A banking source told Reuters that net reserves stood now at $3.5 billion, compared with $2.6 billion cited by the same source at the end of May.
